situation_text: First salary in. The letter said 52,000. The bank says 41,300. HR wants your tax declaration by Friday, and asks if you want to raise your EPF contribution.

options.immediate_text: Less tax deducted. About 1,800 more reaches you each month.
options.deferred_text: Payroll emails you about a correction. You spot it. Nobody else on your team did.

options.option_label: Deal with it in March like everyone else
options.immediate_text: Nothing changes. The extra tax keeps going out.
options.deferred_text: March. You scramble to invest 60,000 you do not have, just to claim a refund.

options.immediate_text: Take home drops to 38,700. The money is not gone, it is locked away.
options.deferred_text: Your retirement balance is 41,000. You have never looked at it before today.

situation_text: You need a place. You have 20,000 saved from before. A studio near office is 18,000. A shared 2BHK is 9,000 for your half. A room 40 minutes out is 6,000.

options.immediate_text: Your own place. Rent is 44% of your take home.
options.deferred_text: A full year gone. Rent has eaten one third of every rupee you earned.

options.immediate_text: Less space, more money, a flatmate you barely know.
options.deferred_text: A year in a place you never invite anyone to. Rent took a fifth of your pay.

options.immediate_text: Cheapest option. Three hours a day belong to the road now.
options.deferred_text: You have stopped going out on weekdays. It is too far to come back into town.

situation_text: Your mother's friend sells insurance. Your parents want you to start a policy. 3,000 a month, pays out after 20 years, small life cover included.

options.immediate_text: Your parents are visibly relieved. The agent shakes your hand.
options.deferred_text: You work out the return. Roughly 4.5% a year, and the life cover is 3 lakhs.

options.immediate_text: Your mother is hurt. Her friend calls twice more.
options.deferred_text: It is still brought up at every family dinner.

options.option_label: Ask what the return and the cover actually are
options.immediate_text: Nobody in the room can answer. Your mother stops talking to you for two days.
options.deferred_text: Your father starts asking the same question about his own policies.

situation_text: A close friend is starting something and needs 25,000. He says three months. You have 38,000 in total.

options.immediate_text: He is grateful. You have 13,000 left.
options.deferred_text: Nine months. He has not mentioned it. Neither have you.

options.option_label: Give 10,000 and call it a gift
options.immediate_text: Smaller help, no repayment expected, no resentment either.
options.deferred_text: He never brought it up. You have not either.

options.immediate_text: He says he understands. The call ends early.
options.deferred_text: He found the money elsewhere. Your conversations are shorter now.

situation_text: Cracked screen, battery dead by 4pm. Repair is 3,000. A decent replacement is 18,000. The one you want is 73,000, or 6,600 a month for twelve months on no-cost EMI.

options.immediate_text: Works fine. Looks bad.
options.deferred_text: Ten months on. It still works. The crack has spread across the top third.

options.immediate_text: Paid for, owned, done.
options.deferred_text: Eight months on. It does everything the 73,000 one does, a little slower.

options.option_label: 6,600 a month for twelve months, no-cost EMI
options.immediate_text: Best phone in the office. 6,600 committed every month for a year.
options.deferred_text: Final EMI paid. The phone is a year old and the new model is out.

situation_text: Your sister wants a coaching class. It costs 8,000. She has not asked your parents. She asked you.

options.immediate_text: She is thrilled. She asks you not to tell your parents.
options.deferred_text: She asks again, for something else. You are the default now.

options.option_label: Pay half, ask her to tell your parents
options.immediate_text: Slightly awkward. Handled in the open.
options.deferred_text: Your parents cover the rest without being asked twice.

options.option_label: Tell her to ask your parents
options.immediate_text: She does. It takes two weeks and a fight.
options.deferred_text: She got the class. She did not come to you again.

situation_text: You can start investing monthly. 5,000 into a broad equity index, 5,000 into a recurring deposit, or wait until you earn more.

options.option_label: 5,000 a month into a broad equity index
options.immediate_text: First investment. A month later it is down 2%.
options.deferred_text: Fourteen months. Four of them were red. The balance is 78,000 on 70,000 put in.

options.option_label: 5,000 a month into a recurring deposit
options.immediate_text: Safe, predictable, about 6.5% a year before tax.
options.deferred_text: It grew exactly as promised. Inflation took most of it.

options.immediate_text: Nothing committed. Full flexibility.
options.deferred_text: A year gone. You are still waiting to earn more.

situation_text: A colleague says he made 40% last year in small companies. He shows you the screen. Your index investment is up 9%.

options.immediate_text: Feels smart. First month it is up 7%.
options.deferred_text: That colleague has stopped mentioning it. Your balance is down 22%.

options.option_label: Keep the index, add small extra there
options.immediate_text: A contained bet. You check it daily now.
options.deferred_text: Down 22%. It was 20,000, not everything.

options.immediate_text: Nothing happens. He brings it up again at lunch, twice, in front of others.
options.deferred_text: He has stopped mentioning it. So has everyone else at lunch.

options.option_label: Start with 30,000 in small caps, like him
options.immediate_text: Feels smart. You check the app before breakfast.
options.deferred_text: Down 22%. You started with 30,000, at the top.

situation_text: Two offers. A large company at 9.5 LPA, stable. A six person startup at 7.3 LPA plus equity you cannot value.

options.immediate_text: Take home jumps by about 18,000. Predictable.
options.deferred_text: A restructure hits your team anyway. Nobody is safe, only slower to fall.

options.immediate_text: Small raise, real ownership, no idea what the equity is worth.
options.deferred_text: Funding does not close. The layoff in month 22 is this decision arriving.

options.immediate_text: Nothing changes. Nothing risked either.
options.deferred_text: Your team is cut anyway.

situation_text: Friday, 3pm. Role eliminated. One month severance. Your monthly costs are 34,000. You have whatever you have.

options.option_label: Cut everything, live off the emergency fund
options.immediate_text: Costs down to 22,000. You calculate your runway daily.
options.deferred_text: Six weeks of runway left. The number has not gone up.

options.immediate_text: 5,000 a month back. The habit breaks in week one.
options.deferred_text: You restarted four months later. Those months never come back.

options.option_label: Put the gap on the credit card
options.immediate_text: Nothing changes day to day. The balance grows quietly.
options.deferred_text: You have a job again. The card balance is still there, and the minimum barely touches it.

options.option_label: Ask your parents to cover you
options.immediate_text: They say yes immediately. You hate it.
options.deferred_text: Handled. It is mentioned at every family gathering for two years.

situation_text: Two months without income. One offer at 6.3 LPA, below what you made. Another process reaches final round in three weeks.

options.immediate_text: Income restarts at a lower number. The bleeding stops.
options.deferred_text: Safe, smaller, and it took three years to get back to where you were.

options.option_label: Wait three weeks for the better process
options.immediate_text: No income, no certainty, one more month of runway gone.
options.deferred_text: It came through at 10.5 LPA. The three weeks had no income at all.

options.immediate_text: Irregular money, long days, no benefits.
options.deferred_text: You kept the runway alive and took the better offer anyway.

situation_text: A cousin is putting money into a scheme paying 3% a month, guaranteed. He has been paid on time for eight months. He wants you in.

options.immediate_text: Three months of payments arrive exactly on time.
options.deferred_text: The payments stop. So does the cousin's phone.

options.option_label: Put in 5,000 just to test it
options.immediate_text: Small amounts come back on schedule. You consider adding more.
options.deferred_text: The scheme collapses. The 5,000 does not come back.

options.option_label: Stay out, and warn your parents
options.immediate_text: Your cousin tells the family you called him a fraud. Your father almost invests anyway.
options.deferred_text: It collapses. Your cousin has not spoken to you since Diwali.
